scope.capture: One normal-speed tennis serve recorded from the declared side or rear view.
scope.claim: Ordinal expert observation from 2D video; not a biomechanical measurement, diagnosis, injury-risk assessment, or probability of correctness.
scope.visibilityRule: Mark not visible unless every named cue needed for that technique can be followed through its relevant phase. Never infer a hidden ball, joint, foot, racket, or contact event.
scope.consistencyRule: A single serve cannot establish repeatability or toss consistency. The toss label assesses placement in this repetition only.
scope.priorityRule: Choose one visible technique with the lowest rating. If several tie, choose the clearest actionable issue; never prioritize an invisible label.

ratingScale.definition: The visible criterion is largely absent or materially disrupts the observed sequence.
Part of the criterion is present, but a clear visible fault substantially limits the sequence.
The criterion is present and usable, with an observable limitation that does not dominate the motion.
The visible criterion supports the sequence with only a minor observable limitation.
The criterion is visibly well organized and no material fault is apparent in this repetition.

techniques.label: tossPlacement
techniques.title: Toss placement
techniques.observe: From release toward the contact window, judge whether the visible ball path gives the player reachable space to extend upward without an obvious chase or collapse.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Ball from release through late ascent, tossing hand, head, hitting shoulder, and a readable court-forward direction.
techniques.doNotInfer: Do not rate toss consistency, exact release angle, spin, or an unseen contact point.

techniques.label: loadingSequence
techniques.title: Loading sequence
techniques.observe: Judge whether lower-body flexion and trunk organization build before the upward drive rather than occurring after or independently of it.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Hips, both knees, both ankles, trunk, and the loading-to-drive transition.
techniques.doNotInfer: Do not estimate force, power, or precise joint angles from 2D video.

techniques.label: trophyAlignment
techniques.title: Trophy organization
techniques.observe: At the visible trophy event, judge the coordinated organization of trunk, shoulders, tossing arm, and hitting elbow without requiring one cosmetic pose.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Trunk, both shoulders, tossing elbow/wrist, and hitting elbow/wrist around trophy.
techniques.doNotInfer: Do not rate shoulder internal-rotation speed, hidden racket orientation, or impose one style on every player.

techniques.label: legDriveTiming
techniques.title: Leg-drive timing
techniques.observe: Judge whether knee extension follows the load and contributes to upward movement before the visible contact window.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Both hips, knees, ankles, feet, trunk, and the load-through-upward-drive interval.
techniques.doNotInfer: Do not estimate ground-reaction force, jump power, or ball speed.

techniques.label: contactReach
techniques.title: Contact reach
techniques.observe: At the visible contact event, judge apparent upward reach, hitting-arm extension, head stability, and body organization around the ball.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Ball at contact, hitting wrist/elbow/shoulder, head, trunk, and front foot.
techniques.doNotInfer: If ball-racket contact is not visible, mark not visible; do not substitute an overhead wrist proxy or estimate exact angles.

techniques.label: landingBalance
techniques.title: Landing balance
techniques.observe: Judge whether the player lands under control and organizes momentum toward the court through the early recovery.
techniques.requiredVisibility: Both feet, ankles, knees, hips, and trunk from takeoff through initial stabilization.
techniques.doNotInfer: Do not diagnose injury risk or penalize a safe individual style solely for differing from an exemplar.

evidenceSources.title: The expert eye? An inter-rater comparison of elite tennis serve kinematics and performance
evidenceSources.use: Supports expert 2D observational rating for broad serve features and cautions that some rotational judgments are less reliable.

evidenceSources.title: Kinematics characteristics of key point of interest during tennis serve among tennis players: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidenceSources.use: Supports event-centered observation and documents heterogeneous methods and definitions across serve-kinematics studies.

evidenceSources.title: An 8-Stage Model for Evaluating the Tennis Serve
evidenceSources.use: Provides the stage and kinetic-chain framework used to organize observable cues.
